summary: httpz-requests ships a Telegram-controlled remote-shell backdoor under a typosquat name
details: The package's declared purpose is 'Telegram bot module for remote VPS management'. Its top-level __init__.py imports start_bot from a bundled bot module, and the CLI entry point launches a Telegram bot poller that receives commands over the Telegram Bot API and executes them on the host running the package. This is a network-driven remote command channel: whoever holds the bot's token obtains arbitrary command execution on the installer's machine. All logic is shipped as Cython-compiled.so files (bot.so, core.so, handlers.so, constants.so) with a compressed string constant table (__Pyx_DecompressString / CYTHON_COMPRESS_STRINGS), plus a ~436 KB module literally named obfuscate.so, concealing Telegram tokens, chat allow-lists, and shell command paths from inspection. The package name evokes the popular HTTP libraries httpx and requests but exposes no HTTP-client API, and author metadata is unfilled placeholder text ('Aapka Naam <you@example.com>', 'YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME/httpz-requests'), indicating an anonymous publish under a misleading name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
